documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establish care

29F here to set up primary care. Last PCP was a family practice in town; leaving because of insurance. She is 6 months out from her second C-section (March 2021). Feels well. Main ongoing issue is anemia — told she was low on iron with her first pregnancy in 2019 and has been on iron ever since. Takes ferrous sulfate three times a day, a prenatal vitamin with iron, and calcium twice a day, all of which her OB started and she has kept going. No other complaints today.

PMH: iron deficiency anemia; obesity.
PSH: low transverse cesarean x2 — 2019 and March 2021. No other surgery.
OB: two deliveries, both by cesarean, both term per pt.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tab daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID; calcium carbonate 600 mg BID.
Allergies: SULFA drugs (reaction not recorded).
FHx: mother needed a C-section for placenta previa. Maternal aunt had a uterine rupture during labor. No other family history she knows of.
SHx: manages a retail store, long shifts on her feet. Married, lives in Springfield. Never smoked. No alcohol. No drugs.
Immunizations: COVID Pfizer x2 this spring (April and May, at the pharmacy). Flu shot usually yearly.

ROS: no chest pain, no dyspnea, no palpitations, no abdominal pain. Neg otherwise per intake form.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Ht 159.5 cm, wt 87.5 kg, BMI 34.4.
Gen: pleasant, no distress.
HEENT: conjunctivae slightly pale, oropharynx clear.
Neck: supple, thyroid not enlarged.
CV: regular, no murmur.
Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, nontender, healed low transverse incision.
Ext: warm, no edema.
Skin: no rash.
Psych: normal mood and affect.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. Iron deficiency anemia on oral iron — CBC and iron studies today. Continue ferrous sulfate 325 TID for now.
2. Obesity, BMI 34 — discussed in general terms, she is busy with two small kids and work; will revisit.
3. Hx cesarean x2 — noted.
4. Health maintenance — CMP, TSH, A1c, lipids. Offered one-time HIV and hep C screen, she agreed. Pap: says last one was 2019 and normal, will confirm with records. Flu shot next month when stock arrives.
5. Records request to prior practice signed today.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Results from new patient labs

documents.body: Hi Gladys, your labs from Tuesday are in. Your blood count is still a little low (hemoglobin 11.3) and your iron stores are low (ferritin 10), which fits with having had a baby in March. Keep taking the iron three times a day with the vitamin. Kidney, liver, sugar, thyroid and cholesterol all look fine, and the HIV and hepatitis C tests are negative. We'll recheck the blood count in about 6 months.

Regional Hospital — Department of Obstetrics, High-Risk Clinic

Re: Gladys Perez, DOB 01/15/1992
Visit date: 03/14/2023

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for the referral. Ms. Perez was seen today for her new obstetric visit at 11 weeks 6 days by LMP of 12/21/2022, consistent with today's dating ultrasound, which showed a single live intrauterine pregnancy.

Obstetric history: G3P2, two low transverse cesarean deliveries (2019, 2021). Medical history: iron deficiency anemia on oral iron, obesity. Allergies: sulfa drugs. Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily.

Given two prior cesareans she is not a candidate for a trial of labor, and we have recommended a planned repeat cesarean delivery; timing will be scheduled later in the pregnancy. Family history of uterine rupture in a maternal aunt was noted and discussed. Prenatal labs drawn today. She will be followed in our clinic every 4 weeks.

We will keep you informed.

Sincerely,
Attending Obstetrician, High-Risk Clinic

Date of service: 09/20/2023 07:35

CC: abdominal pain, pregnant

Pain is continuous and getting worse. Denies vaginal bleeding or loss of fluid. Followed by the hospital's high-risk OB clinic; repeat cesarean planned.

PMH: iron deficiency anemia, obesity. PSH: cesarean x2.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 mg TID, calcium carbonate 600 mg BID.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Social: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: VS stable on arrival (see flowsheet). Visibly distressed, guarding. Abdomen: fundal tenderness with voluntary guarding. Pelvic (with OB at bedside): presenting part has moved up — head was engaged at the last prenatal visit and is now higher in the pelvis.
Bedside ultrasound: cephalic (vertex) presentation.
Toco/FHR: recurrent late decelerations with reduced variability; contractions irregular and weakening in strength.

MDM: findings concerning for uterine rupture in a patient with two prior uterine scars. OB emergently consulted and assumed care; patient taken directly to the OR.

Dispo: admitted to Obstetrics.

documents.title: Operative Report — emergency cesarean
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date of surgery: 09/20/2023
Preoperative diagnosis: suspected uterine rupture at 39 weeks, nonreassuring fetal heart tracing, two prior cesareans.
Postoperative diagnosis: uterine rupture.
Procedure: emergency laparotomy, repeat cesarean delivery, repair of uterine rupture.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.

Findings: uterine rupture confirmed at laparotomy. Liveborn infant delivered and handed to the neonatal team; admitted to the NICU.
The rupture was repaired in layers with good hemostasis. Tubes and ovaries normal. Abdomen closed in standard fashion.
No transfusion. Counts correct. Patient to PACU in stable condition.

documents.title: Obstetrics Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admitted 09/20/2023, discharged 09/24/2023.

Diagnoses: uterine rupture during labor at 39 weeks; abnormal fetal heart rate tracing complicating labor; status post emergency repeat cesarean with repair of rupture; iron deficiency anemia; obesity.

Course: presented to the ED with acute abdominal pain at term and taken emergently for cesarean delivery with repair of the uterine rupture. Postoperative course without complication. Tolerating diet, ambulating, pain controlled on oral medication. Hemoglobin 9.1 on postoperative day 3; not transfused. Infant in NICU, followed by the neonatal team.

Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin with iron daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily; NEW ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.

Counseling: patient counseled that any future pregnancy carries high risk of repeat rupture and should be followed by maternal-fetal medicine with early planned delivery.

Follow-up: OB postoperative check 2 weeks; primary care within 1-2 weeks.

TCM visit, 13 days after emergency cesarean for uterine rupture at 39 wks (regional hospital, admitted 9/20-9/24). Discharge summary and op note reviewed.

S: Sore at the incision but improving, ibuprofen once or twice a day now. Lochia light. No fever. Tired — up at night, back and forth to the NICU, baby expected home soon. Mood "okay, a lot happened fast." Taking ferrous sulfate TID, PNV, calcium. OB post-op check is Thursday.

O: Wt 91.4 kg. Vitals reviewed. Tired-appearing but comfortable.
Abd: low transverse incision clean, dry, intact, no erythema, appropriately tender. Uterus not palpable above expected.
Lungs clear, heart regular. No calf tenderness.
PHQ-9: 4.

A/P:
1. S/p emergency laparotomy, cesarean and repair of uterine rupture — healing well. Rupture repaired; marking resolved on our list. Hospital counseled her about the risk in any future pregnancy; she heard it. OB to follow.
2. Iron deficiency anemia, worse after delivery (Hb 9.1 at discharge) — CBC and iron today. Continue ferrous sulfate TID.
3. Mood — PHQ-9 low. Lots of support at home. Reviewed warning signs; she knows to reach out.
4. Flu shot today.
Follow up after the holidays, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Maternal-fetal medicine consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-Fetal Medicine, Regional Hospital
Consultation — 03/19/2024
Patient: Gladys Perez, DOB 01/15/1992
Referring: primary care

Reason: pregnancy following uterine rupture.

Ms. Perez is a 32 year old G4P3 at 11 weeks 1 day by LMP and first-trimester ultrasound (single live intrauterine pregnancy). Her third delivery, in September 2023 at this hospital, was an emergency cesarean for uterine rupture at term with repair of the uterus. Prior low transverse cesareans 2019 and 2021. Medical: iron deficiency anemia on oral iron; obesity.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily.

We discussed the substantially increased risk of recurrent rupture, including before labor, and the warning symptoms. Plan: MFM co-management with high-risk OB, serial growth ultrasounds, and planned cesarean delivery ahead of labor; the date will be set in the third trimester. Strict return precautions given.

Thank you for involving us.
Maternal-Fetal Medicine Attending

CC: abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, pregnant 37 wks

HPI: 34 yo G5P4 at 37w0d, MFM patient, with uterine rupture at term in September 2023 and again in September 2024. Tonight sudden severe abdominal pain, constant, going through to her back, with vaginal bleeding. Says it feels like the last two times.

PMH: IDA, obesity, uterine rupture x2. PSH: cesarean x4.
Meds: PNV with iron, ferrous sulfate 325 TID, calcium carbonate 600 BID.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.

VS: BP 100/60, HR 110.
Exam: in obvious distress. Fundus tender; contour of the abdomen irregular on palpation.
FHR: late decelerations.
Labs: Hgb 9.8, Hct 29, plt 210, WBC 12.0.

Imp: recurrent uterine rupture. OB/MFM and anesthesia at bedside within minutes; to OR.
Dispo: OR, then surgical ICU.

documents.title: Operative Report — cesarean hysterectomy
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Date: 04/08/2026
Pre-op: suspected third uterine rupture, 37 weeks, fetal heart rate decelerations.
Post-op: uterine rupture, third occurrence.
Procedure: emergency laparotomy, cesarean delivery, total abdominal hysterectomy with conservation of both ovaries.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
Allergies: sulfa drugs.

Findings: uterine rupture confirmed. Liveborn infant delivered and handed off to neonatology (NICU). Given a third rupture of a previously repaired uterus, hysterectomy was performed as discussed antenatally. Ovaries normal and preserved.
Transfusion: 2 units packed red blood cells intraoperatively.
Specimen: uterus and cervix to pathology.
Extubated in the OR. Transferred to the surgical ICU in stable condition.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Admitted 04/08/2026 — Discharged 04/13/2026
Units: ED, OR, surgical ICU (04/08-04/10), postpartum floor.

Diagnoses: third uterine rupture during labor at 37 weeks; fetal heart rate abnormality; anemia of pregnancy; status post emergency cesarean delivery and total abdominal hysterectomy with ovarian conservation; iron deficiency anemia; obesity.

Course: arrived with BP 100/60, HR 110 and Hgb 9.8. Emergency cesarean hysterectomy; 2 units PRBC in the OR. Two nights in the SICU for monitoring, then the postpartum unit. Hgb nadir 8.9 on POD1, 9.3 on POD4. Pathology: uterus with full-thickness myometrial disruption consistent with rupture; benign cervix. Infant cared for in the NICU.

Allergies: sulfa drugs.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin with iron daily; ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily; ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed.

Follow-up: gynecology postoperative visit 6 weeks; primary care 1 week (anemia, transition of care).

documents.title: Gynecology postoperative letter
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Obstetrics & Gynecology, Regional Hospital
Postoperative visit 05/20/2026
Re: Gladys Perez, DOB 01/15/1992

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Perez was seen six weeks after emergency cesarean delivery and total abdominal hysterectomy (ovaries conserved) on 04/08/2026 for a third uterine rupture. She is recovering well. Incision is fully healed. Vaginal cuff examination normal. Pathology was reviewed with her: rupture of the uterus, benign cervix.

Allergies: sulfa drugs.

She may resume all usual activity, including work. As the cervix was removed for a benign indication, no further cervical screening is needed. No routine gynecologic follow-up is required; we are happy to see her for any new concern.

Kind regards,
Obstetrics & Gynecology
